parts.label: (a)
parts.text:

| energy change | always positive | always negative | can be either negative or positive |

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Define standard enthalpy change of atomisation.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Table 3.2 shows some energy changes.

Table 3.2

| energy change | value/$\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| standard enthalpy change of atomisation of silver | +285 |
| first ionisation energy of silver | +731 |
| second ionisation energy of silver | +2074 |
| bond energy of $\text{O=O}$ | +496 |
| bond energy of $\text{O-O}$ | +150 |
| first electron affinity of oxygen | -141 |
| second electron affinity of oxygen | +798 |
| first ionisation energy of oxygen | +1314 |
| standard enthalpy change of formation of silver oxide, $\text{Ag}_2\text{O(s)}$ | -31 |

Calculate the lattice energy, $\Delta H^\ominus_\text{latt}$, of $\text{Ag}_2\text{O(s)}$ using relevant data from Table 3.2.

It may be helpful to draw a labelled energy cycle.

Show your working.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Suggest the trend in the magnitude of the lattice energies of the silver compounds $\text{Ag}_2\text{S}$, $\text{Ag}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{Ag}_2\text{Se}$.

Explain your answer.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.stem: Silver sulfite, $\text{Ag}_2\text{SO}_3\text{(s)}$, is sparingly soluble in water.
parts.text: Give an expression for the solubility product, $K_\text{sp}$, of $\text{Ag}_2\text{SO}_3$.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text:
Calculate the equilibrium concentration of $\text{Ag}^+$ in a saturated solution of $\text{Ag}_2\text{SO}_3$ at $298\text{ K}$.

[$K_\text{sp}$: $\text{Ag}_2\text{SO}_3$, $1.50 \times 10^{-14}\text{ mol}^3\text{dm}^{-9}$ at $298\text{ K}$]

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
The standard enthalpy change of solution, $\Delta H^\ominus_\text{sol}$, of $\text{AgNO}_3\text{(s)}$ in water is $+22.6\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Suggest how the feasibility of dissolving $\text{AgNO}_3\text{(s)}$ in water changes with temperature.

Explain your answer.
